Where this research has entered policy debates, most recent first. Each entry carries what was
being decided, what I contributed, and how it was covered.

### Denmark, 2026 — the food VAT proposal

The government took office on a programme of abolishing VAT on fruit and vegetables and halving
it on other food. Asked by the Folketing Finance Committee whether lower VAT would reach
consumer prices, the Ministry of Finance assembled a table of the literature, cited our 2020
study, and set it aside on the ground that it reports an average across goods rather than a
result for food.

**[Response to the Danish Ministry of Finance on the price effects of a food VAT reduction](memo.pdf)**,
August 2026 — re-estimating the result for food alone and for the kind of rate change Denmark is
proposing, and reviewing the evidence the Ministry assembled.

Coverage: [Jyllands-Posten](https://jyllands-posten.dk/politik/ECE19394802/), interview,
June 2026 ·
[TV 2](https://nyheder.tv2.dk/politik/2026-06-19-forsker-piller-centralt-regeringsforslag-fra-hinanden),
"Forsker piller centralt regeringsforslag fra hinanden", 19 June 2026.

### Japan, 2026–27 — the food consumption-tax cut

Japan is cutting the consumption tax on food from 8 percent to 1 percent for two years from
April 2027.

[Nikkei](https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUA050C00V00C26A7000000/), interview, 7 July 2026 —
「一時的な減税、終了後に物価高騰リスク　消費税にフィンランドの教訓」("Temporary tax cuts risk
higher prices once they end: lessons from Finland for the consumption tax"), on the Finnish
hairdressing experiment and on the Argentine evidence that monitoring limits price increases
when a rate is restored.

Earlier, a [Cabinet Secretariat working
group](https://www.cas.go.jp/jp/seisaku/kokuminkaigi/contents/20260424/minutes.pdf) considering
the cut recorded average pass-through of 13 percent on VAT reductions against 55 percent on
increases, across all EU VAT changes between 1996 and 2015 — alongside the Argentine evidence
that prices settled above their pre-cut level once the tax was restored, except where increases
were regulated.

### Austria, 2026 — the food VAT cut

The [Parliament's
Budgetdienst](https://www.parlament.gv.at/fachinfos/budgetdienst/Senkung-der-Umsatzsteuer-auf-ausgewaehlte-Nahrungsmittel)

### Spain, 2023 — the basic-foods VAT cut

[Nada es
Gratis](https://nadaesgratis.es/miguel-almunia/los-efectos-de-la-reduccion-del-iva-de-los-alimentos-basicos),
March 2023. The reform was also assessed by the European Commission's Joint Research Centre,
*Price Effects of Temporary VAT Rate Cuts: Evidence from Spanish Supermarkets*, and by Banco de
España Working Paper 2417.

### Greece, 2026 — a food VAT cut declined

Greece chose a voluntary supplier price agreement over a rate cut. The small-business institute
IME GSEVEE reviewed the evidence in
[Informational Brief 37](https://imegsevee.gr/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/ioannidis_fpa_2026.pdf),
June 2026, drawing on three of our papers among 32 studies covering 69 VAT episodes. Its own
reading of the most recent episodes differs from ours: it finds cuts in 2022–23 passing through
almost fully, and more fully than increases.

### France, 2018 — the reduced rates under review

In May 2018 the Institut des politiques publiques published our evaluation of the 2009 restaurant
VAT cut, then one of the largest business subsidies in France at around €3bn a year. Ten days
later the Finance Minister said he did not rule out re-examining the reduced rates on restaurants,
housing and transport.

Le Figaro Economie, 28 May · Capital, 29 May · France 2, *Journal de 13h*, 29 May ·
France 3, *19/20*, 29 May · LCI, 30 May · BFM Business, 30 May · Ouest-France, 30 May ·
Economie Matin, 31 May · Les Echos, "Restauration, logement, transport : les taux réduits de TVA
dans le viseur de Le Maire", 7 June · L'Express, "A qui profitent les TVA réduites visées par
Bercy ?", 11 June. Also Alternatives Économiques and Libération.
[IPP brief and press
list](https://www.ipp.eu/en/news/ipp-policy-brief-n32who-benefited-from-the-july-2009-sit-down-restaurant-value-added-tax-cuts/)

Since:
